items.explanation: 30 seconds is 0.5 minute, so the survival probability is e^(−2×0.5).

items.stem: The variance of N(t) for a homogeneous Poisson process is:
items.explanation: A Poisson variable has variance equal to its parameter λt.

items.stem: The time T₃ to the third event has:
items.explanation: T₃ is the sum of three iid Exp(λ) gaps.

items.stem: Which statements are true? A. E[N(t)]=λt. B. Var[N(t)]=λt. C. E[T₁]=λ. D. T₂ is Gamma/Erlang.
items.explanation: A, B and D are true; E[T₁]=1/λ.

A.why: The mean of a Poisson count is its parameter λt.

B.why: The variance of a Poisson count equals its parameter λt.

C.why: The mean first waiting time is 1/λ, not λ.

D.why: The second arrival time is the sum of two iid exponential gaps.

items.stem: A process has rate 5 per hour. What is the probability of at least one event in 12 minutes?
items.explanation: 12 minutes is 0.2 hour; λt=1.

items.stem: For 0≤s<t, the increment N(t)−N(s) has distribution:
items.explanation: The increment count depends on the interval length t−s.

items.stem: Which statements about inter-arrival times are true? A. They are independent. B. They are identically distributed. C. Each has mean λ. D. Each has variance 1/λ².
items.explanation: A, B and D are true; mean is 1/λ.
statements: Each inter-arrival time has mean λ.

A.why: A homogeneous Poisson process has independent increments, yielding independent gaps.

B.why: All gaps have the same Exp(λ) distribution.

items.explanation: The kth event has not happened by t iff at most k−1 events have happened.

items.stem: Which properties hold for a homogeneous Poisson process? A. Stationary increments. B. Independent increments. C. Constant rate. D. Counts in overlapping intervals are independent.
items.explanation: Overlapping intervals share events and are generally dependent.
statements: The process has a constant rate.
Counts in overlapping intervals are independent.

A.why: The increment law depends only on interval length.

B.why: Counts over disjoint intervals are independent.

C.why: Homogeneity means the rate λ is constant over time.

D.why: Overlapping intervals share events, so their counts are generally dependent.

items.stem: A process has rate 6 per hour. Find the probability that the first event occurs within 5 minutes.
items.explanation: Five minutes is 1/12 hour; λt=1/2.
